comments.body: **[P2] Make sure an all-weak row cannot cause a permanent re-run.** If an `unknown` coverage row makes the run `incomplete` (no head marker), then every PR whose tests use `assert.ok`/`toBeTruthy` would re-run the paid review on every push and never get a cached verdict. That is the same failure shape as an unreadable closing issue. As I read it, `unknown` rows give the "❔ … could not be assessed" headline with status `complete`. Please pin that with one assertion in your E1 PR test: `counts.complete === true` and the head marker is present, while the row is `unknown` and the headline is not a clean "No unit test gaps found".

P3: `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` pins a count, so it is a value check for interaction obligations ("sends exactly one email", "retries 3 times"). Classing it as weak downgrades a correctly covered obligation to `unknown`. That is a recall loss, though not noise. I'd move it to `value`, like `toHaveBeenCalledWith(args)`, and keep only bare `toHaveBeenCalled()` as weak. Add a control: `expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` still covers.

Review against probes E1/E2 (from the #199 review).

- E1: one exported classifier shared by both modes. All-weak evidence downgrades the row to `unknown` with a stated reason, and no finding is posted, so there is no new noise. The controls (`toHaveBeenCalledWith`, mixed weak+value, `toThrow(/bad/)`) are the right boundary.
- E2: refutation needs the same normalised EXPR and a different primitive literal in every claim. Different-input and ambiguous claims are untouched, and the refuted finding is gated so #197 cannot re-raise it.
- All 4 tests fail on main. Repointing the two `audit-code` tests to a value assertion is correct, since they modelled exactly the E1 bug.

One P2 (verify no re-run loop) and one P3 (classification) inline.

Good catch, it was a real loop. The new validation note started with `Obligation O1 marked unknown:`, which the reduced-review counter reads as a citation failure. A 1-row PR then counted as 'degraded by validation', so the run became a reduced review, `complete:false`, with no head marker. Fixed in debb50a: the note now says `not covered:`, so it is not counted. New test 'E1 end to end' asserts `counts.complete === true`, the head marker is present, the headline is not 'No unit test gaps found', and the row is unknown. The test failed before the wording fix.
Agreed. `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` is removed from the weak list in debb50a; only bare `toHaveBeenCalled()` stays weak. Control added: `expect(send).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` still covers.

P3, root cause: the fix avoids a regex in `reducedReasons` by changing a note's wording. Completeness now depends on message text. The next person who rewords this note (or adds a similar one) silently brings the loop back. Your end-to-end test would catch it, which is why this is not blocking. The durable fix is to classify by a structured field: push `{ kind: 'weak_evidence' }` (or set a flag on the row) and have `reducedReasons` count only explicit citation-failure kinds, not text matches. Worth a follow-up.

Re-review of debb50a. Both points are resolved.
- P2 was a real re-run loop. `reducedReasons` read the "marked unknown" note as a citation failure, so a one-obligation PR became reduced/incomplete with no head marker. The new end-to-end test pins `complete === true`, the marker present, the row `unknown`, and no clean verdict.
- P3: `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` is now value, with a control.

LGTM; one P3 on the root cause inline. Merging after #216/#217 land.

P3 follow-up: PR mode is tested by mocking the guard and checking its arguments. The probe's actual symptom (a real `missing_test` with `tests/logger.test.js` containing "invalid amount" → demoted, 0 inline) has no end-to-end inverse. One post-level test with the real guard (1 inline, no low-confidence note) would pin it.

Also worth a comment here: a file absent from `test-candidates.txt` passes `undefined` (an unscoped search). Since #210, such a file is in `candidates-cut.txt`, which already makes its `missing_test` low and the run incomplete, so this is safe today. But the safety depends on that ordering.

note: folding the tests' imports into `ver` means a change to a widely shared test helper makes every unit whose tests import it stale at once. **Executing the counterexample is the expensive and risky way to get this.** Running target code from a PR inside the Action means executing untrusted code in a job that holds `GITHUB_TOKEN` and the LLM key. Even "sandboxed opt-in" needs a separate job with no secrets, which is a significant design change.

A cheaper deterministic step covers much of the value first: **statically refute** counterexamples against strict assertions. If the cited assertion is exact equality against a literal (`assert.equal(f(1), 2)`, `toBe(2)`, `toEqual({...})`), a counterexample claiming that some *different* output still passes is false by construction, so demote it. If the assertion is a recognised weak matcher (`ok`, `toBeTruthy`, `toBeDefined`, `toHaveBeenCalled`, `toBeGreaterThan`), the weakness is demonstrated without the model, so it can be labelled *statically supported*. Only the rest stays *model-proposed*.

The three-case test you propose (none / irrelevant low / corroborating high) is covered by #197's tests. Please mark this resolved, or rebase the doc on main.

The mechanism is fixed (#198, #202, #205), but this line's one *remaining* ask is right and is cheap: the scan report should show the funnel as numbers (eligible / inventoried / selected / transmitted whole / verified / deferred-with-reason), so that "complete" can be checked by arithmetic. Today the pieces exist separately (rotation counts, unseen, limitations, not_inventoried) but nowhere add up. I'm treating this as a concrete follow-up.

Agreed, and this is the highest-value open item. Concretely, on main: an `expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalled()` or `assert.ok(result)` line is a real, executed assertion, so it passes `verifyEvidence`. It can then make a *value* obligation ("returns 90 for 100") `covered`. A minimal evidence tier: classify each cited assertion as value / interaction-only / truthiness. A value obligation backed only by interaction or truthiness assertions is at most `weak_test`, never `covered`. This needs no execution, only the matcher name the post-processor already parses. Being reproduced now.

This row has a deterministic instance worth testing without a model: the `covers` guard (`test-map.js` `makeCoverGuard`) demotes a `missing_test` to low when **any** test file contains the cited line's error message or literal. An unrelated test that happens to contain the same string (e.g. a log assertion) would make a real gap disappear from the counted findings. Being reproduced now.

The product invariant here (changed behaviour → falsifiable obligation → executable assertion → trustworthy conclusion, with unavailable context reported honestly) is the right lens. The metamorphic table is the most useful part of the doc.

ci_workflow.content:
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  push: { branches: [main] }
concurrency: { group: "ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}", cancel-in-progress: true }
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: read
  copilot-requests: write
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with: { node-version: 22 }
      - run: node --test src/*.test.js bin/*.test.js eval/*.test.js $(find eval-sandbox -name "*.test.js" 2>/dev/null) # sandbox tests exist only on eval PRs; never run eval/cases fixtures
      - run: diff -r skills/test-review .github/skills/test-review && diff ccr/test-review.instructions.md .github/instructions/test-review.instructions.md
  dogfood:
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with: { fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: ./
        with:
          review_timeout_minutes: "15"
          ignore: eval/cases/
          # content-based discovery would otherwise index this repo's own docs and eval fixtures; only eval-sandbox/** is a requirement source here
          requirements_paths: |
            !docs/**
            !eval/**
            !research/**
            !README.md
            !skills/**
            !.github/**
            !ccr/**
          # TEMPORARY test credential and model (the Copilot quota is used up): remove `|| secrets.SPEC` and the model pin when done (model back to `${{ vars.SPECGUARD_EVAL_MODEL }}`)
          llm_token: ${{ secrets.SPECGUARD_LLM_TOKEN || secrets.SPEC }}
          model: haiku-5.5
          max_comments: "${{ vars.SPECGUARD_EVAL_MAX_COMMENTS || '10' }}"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        with: { name: specguard-ctx, path: .specguard-ctx/, retention-days: 7, include-hidden-files: true }
